---
title: "Train and monitor a surrogate"
---

Once your data are ready, train through Python as in the
[quickstart](../package/quickstart.qmd), or use Hydra:

```bash
uv run metis train model=mlp training.steps=1000 plot.enabled=true
```

This uses the bundled example. Set `dataset=parquet` and its column names for
your own bank, following [the Hydra guide](../package/hydra.qmd).

Each run saves the configuration, training history, model and evaluation:
`config.yaml`, `history.json`, `model.pt` and `metrics.json`. With the `[plots]`
extra installed, `plot.enabled=true` also saves `evaluation.png`.

## The main controls

| Setting | What it changes |
|---|---|
| `training.steps` | Number of optimizer updates, not epochs |
| `training.batch_size` | Realisations sampled for each update |
| `training.learning_rate` | Size of the optimizer's updates |
| `training.eval_every` | How often validation is checked |
| `training.patience` | Validation checks without improvement before stopping |

Training uses AdamW and keeps the best evaluated weights. Compare model families
using validation prediction errors; their training losses have different meanings.

## Faster or longer runs

The default is CPU training in float32 with a constant learning rate. For a
warm-up followed by cosine decay:

```bash
uv run metis train training.schedule=warmup_cosine
```

For a compatible CUDA setup:

```bash
uv run metis train training.device=cuda training.precision=bf16
```

See [CUDA installation](../basics/installing_metis.qmd#optional-cuda-setup),
[multiple devices](../utils/distributed-training.qmd),
[checkpoints](saving-and-loading.qmd) and
[W&B tracking](../package/hydra.qmd#live-tracking) when you need them.
